tasks.title: Implement schema v3: kind discriminator, stint refs, v2 to v3 migration, stint files
tasks.description:
Context: Foundational schema change for add-stints, change #3 of 4. Post-merge state ASSUMES improve-cli-ergonomics (scoped move/edit/assign) and add-event-log-and-status (event log, status, structured claim with claimedAt) are merged and working. Current schema is v2; store.Load (internal/store/store.go:128-145) decodes version+tasks in one DisallowUnknownFields pass, so the clear version-gate message becomes unreachable once unknown fields like kind/ref appear. Implements openspec tasks 1.1-1.6; the dedicated test suite is a separate follow-up lap (task 1.7).

Outcome: Queue entries carry a `kind` discriminator (`lap` default, `stint`); a stint-ref entry reuses the envelope plus `ref` and orders by the same order key. CurrentVersion becomes 3. v2 files migrate by stamping kind:"lap" on every entry and bumping version, AFTER the existing v1->v2 ordering migration. Future-version files surface the clear version-gate message (not a generic unknown-field error). Stints live at .laps/stints/<name>.laps.json; archive dir at .laps/stints/archive/. Stint names are file-safe; archive moves are no-overwrite.

Files & scope: internal/store/store.go (Task +kind; stint-ref shape or kind switch on Task; CurrentVersion=3; Load decode-order; migrate extended to v2->v3; stint-name validation; archive path + no-overwrite helpers). Do not touch internal/cmd command surface (later laps) or claim.go structured fields (lap 11).

Design: Three subtleties. (1) Decode order is the core of task 1.3: do a LENIENT first decode of just the version envelope, run the version gate, THEN strict-decode entries. Otherwise a future v4 file fails with the generic unknown-field error instead of the clear update-laps message (design.md Risks). (2) Migration ordering: v1->v2 ordering migration THEN v2->v3 kind stamping, in that order, both idempotent; a no-kind entry is a lap by default. (3) Stint names are file names not paths: reject blank, os.PathSeparator, `.`, `..`, and collisions with active OR archived stint files. Archive moves MUST check target absence before os.Rename. Preserve Save's Normalize invariant.

Acceptance: `just build` and `just lint` clean. Existing internal/store/store_test.go and ordering_test.go pass UNCHANGED (the migration/version-gate behavior they pin down is preserved, not regressed). Smoke: hand-craft a v2 file, load it, observe version=3 with kind:"lap" stamped on every entry.

tasks.title: Write schema v3 test suite
tasks.description:
Context: Lap 1 implemented schema v3. This lap adds the dedicated coverage called out in task 1.7, split from impl because migration and version-gate correctness is subtle and high-risk.

Outcome: internal/store has thorough, named tests covering every scenario in task 1.7.

Files & scope: internal/store/store_test.go (extend) or a new internal/store/stint_test.go if cleaner. No production code changes unless a tiny one-liner is needed to make a test possible.

Design: Tests must assert the decode-order guarantee EXPLICITLY: a synthetic v4 file (CurrentVersion+1) carrying a novel entry field produces the version-gate error string, NOT the generic unknown-field error. Migration tests must verify BOTH steps (v1->v2 ordering, v2->v3 kind stamping) run in order and are idempotent. The mixed-queue test must verify laps and stint refs round-trip and order by their order keys together. Name-safety tests must cover each rejection branch (blank, separator, `.`, `..`, active collision, archived collision) and the archive no-overwrite case.

Acceptance: `just test` green. Each task-1.7 scenario has at least one named test. `just lint` clean.

tasks.title: Implement globally-unique lap ids via stint prefixes
tasks.description:
Context: Schema v3 is in. Today store.GenerateID (internal/store/store.go:413) builds `<repo-prefix>-<hash>` where repo-prefix is the first 4 lowercase alphanumerics of the repo dir name (normalizePrefix, store.go:429), so ids are unique only within a file. To make a lap id globally unique AND self-identify its owning queue, each stint gets its own 4-char prefix allocated once at creation and recorded in stint file metadata; laps inside a stint use the stint prefix, root laps keep the repo prefix. Implements tasks 1.8 and 1.9 with bundled tests (the prefix surface is narrow enough to bundle).

Outcome: store.GenerateID takes the containing scope's prefix. Stint file metadata records its allocated 4-char prefix. Allocation: first 4 lowercase alphanumerics of the stint name, made unique against the repo prefix and all existing stint prefixes by trying other permutations/substrings of the name chars, then incrementing the last char through 0-9a-z. A lap id's prefix maps directly to its owning stint (or root), so scoped explicit-id resolution and the active-lap marker can identify scope from the id alone.

Files & scope: internal/store/store.go (GenerateID signature change to accept scope prefix; normalizePrefix reuse; new AllocateStintPrefix helper; stint metadata prefix field). Update all GenerateID call sites in internal/cmd to pass the correct scope prefix. A minimal stints new skeleton in internal/cmd/stints.go may be needed to exercise allocation (the full command surface lands in lap 16).

Design: Two subtleties. (1) The GenerateID signature change ripples to every caller: root callers pass normalizePrefix(repoRoot), stint callers pass the stint's recorded prefix. Keep the existing hash + numeric-suffix collision-extension behavior intact. (2) Allocation uniqueness MUST check BOTH the repo prefix AND all existing stint prefixes (read prefix metadata across .laps/stints/). The permutation/substring fallback MUST stay deterministic (sorted candidate list) so the same name + existing set always yields the same prefix. Widening to 6 chars is explicitly a non-goal here.

Acceptance: `just build`, `just test`, `just lint` clean. New tests: stint laps carry the stint prefix; root vs stint ids never collide; a name whose first-4 collides with the repo prefix or an existing stint prefix gets a distinct allocated prefix; allocation is deterministic across runs with identical inputs.

tasks.title: VERIFY Phase A: schema v3 and globally-unique id prefixes
tasks.description:
Context: Phase A complete (laps 1-3). HIGH-RISK: schema v3 migration is one-way and id-prefix allocation correctness underpins every downstream scope-resolution guarantee. Use the openspec-verify-change skill against the `add-stints` change.

Files & scope: Read-only review. Identify the branch/merge target BEFORE diffing (check PR metadata, branch config, recent git history; do not assume main). Diff <target>...HEAD for the Phase A changes.

Design: Do not rewrite git history; if cleanup is needed, add a focused head lap instead. Tests-green is NOT sufficient verification here. Trace the actual code paths: (a) store.Load lenient envelope decode -> version gate -> strict entry decode (confirm a synthetic v4 file hits the version-gate message, not the unknown-field error); (b) migrate v1->v2->v3 ordering and idempotency; (c) kind/ref shapes and ordering with laps; (d) stint-name validation branches and archive no-overwrite; (e) GenerateID signature + every caller passes the correct scope prefix; (f) AllocateStintPrefix determinism and that the uniqueness set includes BOTH the repo prefix AND existing stint prefixes. If improve-cli-ergonomics or add-event-log-and-status work appears in the diff, treat it as pre-existing baseline unless the user asks otherwise.

Acceptance: Report states what is correct, what is missing, and any blockers. Check 1.1-1.9 boxes in openspec/changes/add-stints/tasks.md for verified-done work. Open head laps for any gap too big for a one-liner fix.

tasks.title: VERIFY raw stint-file prefix enforcement for Phase A
Fix raw stint-file initialization to require/assign stint prefixes
Implement read-through resolution: descend through active stint refs
tasks.description:
Context: Schema v3 + id prefixes are verified in. Now the resolution layer that makes stints invisible to agents. From the root head, descend through active stint refs to the first lap; recursive for nesting. Route get/claim/done/list through it; keep agent output identical. Classify resolver failures. Implements tasks 2.1, 2.2, 2.3. Tests are a separate lap (task 2.4).

Outcome: A resolver that takes the root File and returns the resolved deepest-active context (file path + canonical scope string + head lap). get/claim/done/list use it and produce agent-identical output (title/description only, no nesting indication). Resolver failures (missing child file, malformed stint ref, malformed child file, cycle) error deterministically rather than loop or silently skip.

Files & scope: A new internal/store/resolution.go (or internal/cmd/resolver.go, wherever File loading naturally lives) for the resolver. internal/cmd/get.go, claim.go, done.go, list.go route through it. count.go and prune.go are NOT flow ops: they get scope-flag handling in lap 7, NOT recursive descent.

Design: CRITICAL TRAP (design.md Canonical scope strings): the cycle-detection visited set MUST key on PHYSICAL stint identity (the ref name / resolved child-file path), NOT the slash-path scope string. A cumulative slash path is unique on every descent (A, A/B, A/B/A, ...) so a path-keyed set NEVER detects an A->B->A cycle and loops forever. The ref name / child-file path is constant per stint regardless of where it sits in the path, so keying on that catches the revisit. This is the single most important correctness invariant in this lap. Second subtlety: agent output stays identical, get returns title/description only with no nesting hint. Third: failure classes must be distinguishable so commands surface the right error.

Acceptance: `just build`, `just test`, `just lint` clean. Smoke: with a stint ref at root head, `laps get` returns the stint's head lap with no nesting hint; nested stints descend recursively; synthetic-cycle input errors cleanly without looping.

tasks.title: Write resolver test suite
tasks.description:
Context: Lap 5 built the resolver. The cycle-detection keying trap is subtle enough to warrant a dedicated test lap. Implements task 2.4.

Outcome: Named tests for: get descends into the active stint; recursion across a nested stint; each failure class (missing child file, malformed ref, malformed child file, cycle) errors without looping or silently skipping.

Files & scope: internal/store or internal/cmd test file (wherever the resolver lives). No production changes unless a tiny one-liner is needed.

Design: The cycle test MUST construct an actual A->B->A ref graph (two stint files whose refs point at each other) and assert the command fails with a cycle error and mutates no file. This is the regression that would catch a path-keyed visited set. The test author should confirm by reasoning that the test catches the bug, not pass by accident. Failure-class tests should assert the error message distinguishes the class (missing child vs malformed ref vs malformed child vs cycle).

Acceptance: `just test` green. Each task-2.4 scenario has a named test. `just lint` clean.

tasks.title: Implement scope flags: --active/-c, --root/-r, --stint/-s
tasks.description:
Context: Resolver is in. Now the operator-facing scope vocabulary. Shared local, mutually-exclusive flags on queue-targeting commands. Implements tasks 3.1, 3.2, 3.3, and the flag-leak reset-harness update (3.5). Scoped-op semantics land in the next lap; this lap is flag wiring + path resolution + harness only.

Outcome: Queue-targeting commands (add, get, claim, done, list, count, delete, prune, move, edit, assign) accept --active/-c (default), --root/-r, --stint <name>/-s. Two scope flags combined errors. Raw --file plus any scope flag errors. --stint resolves to .laps/stints/<name>.laps.json via a DEDICATED stint-path helper distinct from ResolveFile. Non-queue commands (init, on, off, update, version, help, log, status, hook-only) reject or omit these flags. The runMB/runMBExecute reset harness resets the new flag sets so a --root/--stint set in one test does not leak Changed=true into the next.

Files & scope: internal/cmd/root.go or a new internal/cmd/scope.go for shared flag registration + the stint-path helper. Each queue-targeting command file for MarkFlagsMutuallyExclusive wiring. internal/cmd/cmd_test.go runMB (cmd_test.go:33-54) and runMBExecute (cmd_test.go:89-118) reset-list extension. Do NOT conflate with hooks.go isKnownCommand (that is lap 16).

Design: CRITICAL (task 3.3): --active is the default but MUST be implemented as a flag detected via .Changed, NOT a default-true value, or cobra's MarkFlagsMutuallyExclusive will false-positive on every invocation. For the --file mutex: per queue-targeting command, MarkFlagsMutuallyExclusive("file", "root", "stint", "active"); the persistent file flag is visible in each command's merged flag set. The stint-path helper is NOT ResolveFile: -f auth -> .laps/auth.json, but --stint auth -> .laps/stints/auth.laps.json (different dir + .laps.json infix). Task 3.5: today's hardcoded reset list (rootCmd.PersistentFlags, addCmd, listCmd, updateCmd, doneUndoCmd) does not cover the new shared scope-flag package vars, the per-command local flag sets, or the stints subcommand flag sets; extend the list (or replace it with a recursive walk of all command flag sets) so Changed state resets between tests.

Acceptance: `just build`, `just test`, `just lint` clean. Smoke: each scope flag works alone; combining two errors; --file + scope flag errors; a --root set in test A does not leak into test B. The full task-3.4 matrix lands in lap 9.

tasks.title: Implement scoped structure ops and delete --force
tasks.description:
Context: Scope flags are wired. Now structure-op semantics: default to active scope, resolve explicit ids within scope, out-of-scope error names the stint. Plus delete --force on claimed laps. Implements tasks 4.1, 4.2, 4.3. Task 10.1 (confirm improve-cli-ergonomics landed for scoped move/edit/assign) is the FIRST step of this lap.

Outcome: add/move/edit/assign/delete default to active scope. Every id-taking queue command (get, claim, done, add after, move, edit, assign, delete) resolves the id within the selected scope first; if the id lives in another stint, the command fails with a message NAMING that stint and mutates no file. delete --force removes a claimed lap and clears the matching claim; default delete refuses a claimed lap with a stderr warning.

Files & scope: internal/cmd/add.go, move.go, edit.go, assign (the claim shortcut), delete.go, get.go, done.go. internal/store for any scope-aware id-lookup helper.

Design: FIRST step is task 10.1: verify move/edit/assign commands exist (improve-cli-ergonomics dependency). If they are missing, do NOT stub them; add a head lap flagging the blocker and stop. Assuming present: the out-of-scope error must NAME the stint (example: `a7 is in stint search - re-run with -s search`), not just say not-found. Use the id-prefix -> stint map from lap 3 to locate the owning stint in O(1). DECIDED (design.md Deleting claimed laps): delete is the ONLY guarded structural case. Default delete refuses a claimed lap; --force removes it and clears the matching claim. Completing a claimed lap via done is allowed and NOT guarded (concurrency is a Non-Goal; the single-actor structural guarantee is sufficient). Keep add-after root-structural semantics; root-only resolution for `stints enqueue after` lands in lap 11.

Acceptance: `just build`, `just test`, `just lint` clean. Smoke: add head into active stint; add --root into root; out-of-scope id errors name the stint; claimed delete refuses; forced claimed delete clears the claim. Full task-4.4 tests land in lap 9.

tasks.title: Implement claim scope and enqueue/preemption
tasks.description:
Context: Scope flags + scoped ops verified. Now preemption-safety (claim records its scope) and the enqueue command. Implements tasks 5.1, 5.2, 5.4, 6.1, 6.2, 6.3, 6.4. Tests are a separate lap (tasks 5.5, 6.5).

Outcome: Claim record becomes {lap, file, scope, claimedAt} with back-compat reads for older claims lacking scope. Bare `laps done` resolves the claimed lap within its RECORDED scope, regardless of current head (preemption-safe). Claim JSON parsing tolerates future fields. `laps stints enqueue <name> [head|tail|after <id>]` inserts a stint ref into the root queue via ComputeInsertOrder, default tail. head preempts the active stint non-destructively (each stint's progress lives in its own file; the paused stint resumes when the interloper drains). `after <id>` resolves ONLY in root; if the id exists only inside a stint, fail naming that stint. Empty stints are ordinary stint files with no special empty-stint state.

Files & scope: internal/store/claim.go (add scope field, back-compat read, future-field tolerance review of any DisallowUnknownFields). internal/cmd/claim.go and done.go (bare done uses recorded scope). internal/cmd/stints.go (enqueue subcommand using ComputeInsertOrder at root). internal/store/store.go (stint-ref insertion helper if cleaner).

Design: DECIDED (design.md Claim records scope): the single-actor structural guarantee is sufficient. A claimed todo lap blocks its stint from draining (drain = no todo laps), so under one actor doing claim->done the recorded scope file always still exists when bare done looks. Concurrency is a Non-Goal: an explicit `done <id>` or a second session MAY drain+archive the stint leaving a stale claim, accepted, not guarded (delete is the only guard, already in lap 8). Preemption is non-destructive BECAUSE each stint's progress lives in its own file: there is no separate pause write; the preempted stint simply resumes from its file when the interloper's ref drains. `after` is root-queue structural work: resolve in root only; if the id exists only in a stint, fail naming that stint (design.md Explicit id resolution).

Acceptance: `just build`, `just test`, `just lint` clean. Smoke: claim records scope; bare done after enqueue head completes the ORIGINALLY-claimed lap (not the new head); enqueue tail default; enqueue head preempts; after root-only resolution fails naming the stint; empty stint enqueues. Tasks 5.5, 6.5 tests land in lap 12.

Files & scope: internal/cmd/cmd_test.go and/or internal/store/claim_test.go. No production changes.

Design: The preemption-safety test is the headline: claim a lap in stint A, enqueue stint B at head, bare done; assert A's claimed lap completes (not B's head). The future-field tolerance test feeds claim JSON with an extra unknown field and asserts it parses cleanly. The resume test enqueues B at head, does one lap in B, drains B, then asserts A's remaining progress is intact and resolvable.

Acceptance: `just test` green. Each task-5.5 and task-6.5 scenario has a named test. `just lint` clean.

tasks.title: Implement drain, auto-archive, and cross-stint done undo
tasks.description:
Context: Claim scope + enqueue implemented. Now the HIGH-RISK stint lifecycle: drain detection, auto-archive with partial-failure-safe ordering, and cross-stint done undo. Implements tasks 7.1, 7.2, 7.3, 7.4. Tests are a separate lap (task 7.5).

Outcome: When a stint has no todo laps left, the draining operation flips its ref to done (sets completedAt) and moves the stint file to .laps/stints/archive/. Draining is content-based and position-independent (a preempted, non-head stint still drains). `laps done undo` scans ALL queue files (root, active stints, .laps/stints/archive/) for the greatest CompletedAt and reopens that lap; if it is in an archived stint, undo restores the stint file to .laps/stints/, reopens the root stint ref (clears completedAt), then reopens the lap under the existing undo rules (5-minute age gate still applies).

Files & scope: internal/cmd/done.go (drain detection on the emptying operation; partial-failure-safe archive ordering; done undo cross-file scan replacing done.go:114-123 single-file max). internal/store/store.go (archive path helpers from lap 1; all-file scan helper if cleaner).

Design: HIGH-RISK partial-failure ordering (design.md Ordering and partial-failure). The drain spans up to three non-transactional writes: (1) complete the lap in the stint file, (2) flip+save the root ref, (3) os.Rename into archive/. Order them FAIL-SAFE: check the archive-collision (no-overwrite) AND target writability BEFORE any mutation; then complete the lap; then os.Rename LAST; then flip the root ref to done ONLY after the rename succeeds. Contract if rename still fails (e.g. crash): the lap completion stands, the ref stays todo, and the next flow op re-attempts the drain on the now-empty stint (drain is content-based, so idempotent). NEVER leave a done root ref over a still-present non-archived stint file (that would mishandle stints ls/rm archived-with-done-ref matrix). Cross-stint undo (DECIDED, design.md): scan all queue files deterministically (NOT the best-effort event log); greatest CompletedAt wins; the archived-stint case restores file + reopens ref + reopens lap; the 5-min age gate still applies. The scan relies on lap ids being globally unique (lap 3), so there is no ambiguity about which file owns the latest completion.

Acceptance: `just build`, `just test`, `just lint` clean. Smoke: completing the last lap drains + archives (ref flipped, file moved); a non-head stint drains; undo after archive unarchives + reopens the ref + reopens the lap; an archive collision is refused without overwriting. Task 7.5 tests land in lap 14.

tasks.title: Write drain and cross-stint undo test suite
tasks.description:
Context: Lap 13 implemented drain + auto-archive + cross-stint undo, the highest-risk lap in this change. Dedicated test lap. Implements task 7.5.

Outcome: Named tests for: completing the last lap drains and archives (ref flipped to done, file moved to archive); a non-head/preempted stint drains correctly (content-based, position-independent); undo after archive unarchives the stint file, reopens the root ref, and reopens the lap; archive collision is refused without overwriting; partial-failure ordering (simulate a non-writable archive or a pre-existing archive target and assert the lap completion stands but no done-ref-over-present-file state is left).

Files & scope: internal/cmd/cmd_test.go and/or internal/store. No production changes.

Design: The partial-failure test is the subtle one. Make the archive target non-writable or pre-existing and assert: (a) the lap completion in the stint file is preserved, (b) the root ref is NOT flipped to done, (c) no done-ref-over-present-file state remains. This catches the core drain-ordering bug. The non-head drain test catches the drain-is-position-based regression. The undo-unarchive test must assert all three reopens (file restored, ref reopened, lap reopened) and that the 5-min age gate still applies.

Acceptance: `just test` green. Each task-7.5 scenario has a named test, INCLUDING the partial-failure ordering test. `just lint` clean.

tasks.title: Implement stints commands, st alias, list --tree, and rm safety
tasks.description:
Context: Drain + undo verified. Now the full command surface. Implements tasks 8.1, 8.2, 8.3, 8.4, 8.5, 8.6, 8.7 (tests bundled: the commands are mostly Cobra wiring around already-built infrastructure; the rm safety matrix is the subtle part and is covered explicitly in acceptance).

Outcome: `laps stints ls|new <name>|enqueue <name> [head|tail|after <id>]|show <name>|rm <name> [--force]` all work; `st` aliases `stints`. stints ls lists stint files with lap counts and a queued indicator; unqueued stints show as ordinary files with queued=false (no draft/lifecycle state). list --tree renders the full recursive overview. Non-tree list renders a stint-ref entry as a single line: `<n>. <name>/ (stint - <N> laps[, held])` (design.md list rendering) so a mixed queue is legible without --tree. internal/cmd/hooks.go:isKnownCommand treats stints and st as built-ins (task 8.6). stints rm: removes unqueued non-archived and archived stints (including archived with a done ref); refuses non-archived queued/active/claimed stints unless --force; forced removal removes matching root refs AND clears matching claims.

Files & scope: internal/cmd/stints.go (full subcommand surface; enqueue and the new skeleton come from earlier laps). internal/cmd/list.go (--tree rendering + stint-ref line rendering). internal/cmd/hooks.go:isKnownCommand (add stints + st). internal/cmd/root.go (st alias registration).

Design: stints rm safety matrix is the subtle part (design.md stints rm safety). Default allows: unqueued non-archived + archived (INCLUDING archived with a done root ref). Default refuses: non-archived queued/active/claimed. --force removes the stint file AND matching root refs AND clears matching claims. The archived-with-done-ref case is explicitly allowed by default (natural cleanup path). Unqueued stints are NOT a separate lifecycle state: ordinary stint files with queued=false and normal counts. The st alias MUST route through the same subcommands (test via runMBExecute per task 8.7). list --tree descends recursively through active stint refs for the full nested overview.

Acceptance: `just build`, `just test`, `just lint` clean. Task 8.7 tests bundled: stints lifecycle commands; st alias through runMBExecute; --tree rendering; rm safety matrix incl. --force, archived-with-done-ref, and claim clearing; unqueued display/state behavior. The list-rendering decision (id-based active marker, unambiguous because ids are globally unique via lap 3) is exercised by the --tree and mixed-queue tests.

tasks.title: Implement log/status scope integration and hook $scope
tasks.description:
Context: Stints commands complete. Now integration with the event log, status, and hooks (all from add-event-log-and-status). Implements tasks 9.1, 9.2, 9.3, 9.4, 9.5 (tests bundled).

Outcome: Event-log entries carry the resolved scope (canonical slash path: root, auth, auth/search). New events: stint.enqueued, stint.completed, stint.archived. status reports the active stint and per-stint progress. Hook vars under scoped operations: $file is the resolved physical task file and $scope is the canonical logical scope. The hook-only (unknown-command) path either gains $scope defaulting to root OR documents that hook-only commands do not receive $scope (one chosen, implemented consistently).

Files & scope: internal/cmd/hooks.go:buildHookVars (hooks.go:53) adds $scope. internal/cmd/root.go:96-105 (the hook-only vars map built inline, bypassing buildHookVars) gets $scope=root or a documented omission. internal/store or internal/cmd event-logging path adds scope to events and the three stint.* event types. internal/cmd/status.go (from add-event-log-and-status) reports active stint + per-stint progress.

Design: Canonical scope strings everywhere (design.md Canonical scope strings + spec): `root`, root-level stint names, slash paths for nesting (auth/search). CRITICAL: the cycle-detection visited set from lap 5 is a SEPARATE concept and MUST NOT use the slash-path string. Do not conflate the canonical scope string with the visited-set key. Hook-only path decision (task 9.3): the inline vars map at root.go:96-105 bypasses buildHookVars. Either add $scope=root there, or document explicitly that hook-only commands do not receive $scope. Pick one and apply it consistently across the code and tests. stint.completed fires on drain; stint.archived fires on the archive move; stint.enqueued fires on enqueue.

Acceptance: `just build`, `just test`, `just lint` clean. Task 9.5 tests bundled: scope reflects the stint; stint events logged; status shows the active stint; hook variables under a scoped done include $scope; nested scope encoding uses slash paths (auth/search).

tasks.title: Document stints, scope flags, and id prefixes in README
tasks.description:
Context: All implementation complete. Docs lap. Implements tasks 10.1 (record improve-cli-ergonomics dependency resolution), 11.1 (README), 11.2 (no VERSION bump).

Outcome: README documents stints, the scope flags (--active/-c, --root/-r, --stint/-s), `laps stints`, `list --tree`, the claim `scope` field, and the per-stint id-prefix scheme (lap ids are globally unique and their prefix encodes their owning stint). VERSION is NOT bumped (add-stints-gating owns the final 0.9.0 bump). The improve-cli-ergonomics dependency is recorded as resolved (or routed to follow-up if lap 8 found it still open).

Files & scope: README.md only. Do NOT touch VERSION. Do NOT touch openspec/.

Design: Match existing README tone and structure. The per-stint id-prefix section should explain that a lap id's prefix identifies its owning stint (or root), so scoped explicit-id resolution and the active-lap marker work unambiguously. The scope-flags section should cover --active/-c (default, descends), --root/-r (no descent), --stint <name>/-s (named, no descent) and the mutual-exclusion rules (including raw --file). Note that bare verbs used by agents default to --active and descend; operators use the long forms for explicit structural control. Keep the schema-v3 note factual: on-disk schema reaches v3 while the binary VERSION stays 0.8.1 until add-stints-gating bumps 0.9.0.

Acceptance: README renders cleanly. VERSION unchanged at 0.8.1. `just build` still clean (docs-only).

tasks.description:
Context: All implementation + docs complete. Final full-change verification. Use the openspec-verify-change skill against `add-stints`.

Outcome: Verified report on the ENTIRE add-stints change. Check off ALL remaining tasks.md boxes (8.1-8.7, 9.1-9.5, 10.1, 11.1, 11.2) ONLY if thoroughly and correctly done. Confirm no boxes were ticked by implementation laps.

Files & scope: Read-only review of the whole diff. Identify the branch/merge target BEFORE diffing (<target>...HEAD). Run `just test`, `just lint`, `just build` end to end. Trace every core dependency line end-to-end: schema v3 decode-order -> migration -> id-prefix allocation -> resolver (cycle keying on PHYSICAL stint identity) -> scope flags (--active via .Changed) -> scoped ops (out-of-scope names the stint) -> claim scope (preemption-safe bare done) -> enqueue (head non-destructive) -> drain (partial-failure ordering) -> undo (all-file scan + unarchive + ref reopen + lap reopen) -> commands (rm safety matrix incl. archived-with-done-ref and --force claim clearing) -> log/status (canonical slash-path scope strings, $scope hook var, hook-only path decision) -> docs.

Design: Do not rewrite history. Pre-existing dependency work (improve-cli-ergonomics, add-event-log-and-status) in the diff is baseline: flag as pre-existing, do not add cleanup laps unless the user explicitly asks. The four invariants to re-confirm one more time: (1) resolver visited-set keying on physical stint identity, not slash-path scope; (2) drain partial-failure ordering never leaves a done root ref over a still-present non-archived stint file; (3) id-prefix global uniqueness (root + all stint prefixes); (4) --active detected via .Changed, not default-true. If any is wrong, open a head lap rather than fixing inline beyond a safe one-liner.

Acceptance: Full report. All tasks.md boxes for add-stints checked (or gaps flagged with head laps). `just test`, `just lint`, `just build` all green. VERSION still 0.8.1. Confirm no implementation lap ticked a tasks.md box.
